title: Two Natchez Trace stops near Pontotoc to visit as Tupelo’s visitor center closes for Thanksgiving
excerpt: Tockshish and the Chickasaw Council House marker are 1.5 miles apart on the parkway. The visitor center near Tupelo closes Thanksgiving Day, and southbound travelers face a detour in Attala County.

paragraphs.text: Thanksgiving visitors can find two outdoor history stops just a mile and a half apart on the Natchez Trace Parkway near Pontotoc. Tockshish is at milepost 249.6 and the Chickasaw Council House marker is at 251.1. Anyone planning to pick up a map or talk with a ranger at the main visitor center near Tupelo should do that on another day. The building closes Thursday, Nov. 26.

Tockshish tells the story of a settlement that became the second post office between Nashville and Natchez in 1801. Riders carrying the mail changed horses there. The original post office is gone. The park service lists parking and wheelchair access at the interpretive stop.

The Council House marker points west, toward the old trail and the Chickasaw village of Pontatock. Its council house served as the capital of the Chickasaw Nation in the 1820s. Leaders met there to make laws and policy and sign treaties. Visitors will find an interpretive marker at the parkway stop. The council house itself no longer stands.

The visitor center is farther north at milepost 266. Its usual hours are 9 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and it has maps, a short paved trail nearby and picnic tables. For those driving south toward central Mississippi, the park service’s Nov. 19 update lists a construction closure in Attala County between mileposts 159.5 and 165. The signed detour uses Mississippi 12 and Mississippi 19/35. The park service advises long-distance cyclists to arrange transport around that section.
